heading: Thursday, September 3, 2026
topLine: OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra claims infinitely many consecutive primes at most 186 apart. Also: OpenAI launches GPT-6 Astra.

items.headline: OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra claims infinitely many consecutive primes at most 186 apart
items.summary: With the GPT-6 Astra launch, OpenAI released a paper (dated 30 August) proving DHL[40,2], which implies infinitely many pairs of consecutive primes differ by at most 186. This improves the Polymath bound of 246 and Julia Stadlmann's concurrent 240, and the paper attributes the proof to GPT-6 Astra. The accompanying Lean formalization depends on three stated axioms: cited Kloosterman-sum estimates and numerical integral bounds that are checked separately in Python. No independent human review had been reported, and the twin prime conjecture is untouched.

items.headline: OpenAI launches GPT-6 Astra
items.summary: GPT-6 Astra is OpenAI's most capable broadly deployed model and the first it rates as reaching Critical cybersecurity capability under its Preparedness Framework, released in phases starting with select organizations before paid ChatGPT plans and the API. OpenAI claims state-of-the-art computer-use and coding results; API pricing is $10/$50 per million input/output tokens.
